source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne CIN5 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 400,000 square feet of technical space in Lebanon, Ohio. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 12 MW supports roughly 300 racks, and at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it supports roughly 1,200 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's claim. The 400,000 square feet is large relative to the 12 MW figure, which implies the campus was built for lower-density workloads and may have limited headroom for the high-density cooling that GPU clusters require.

The certifications qualify the campus for specific regulated workloads. SOC 2 Type 2 and SSAE 16 Type II attest to audited operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. FISMA qualifies it for certain federal information systems. ISO 27001 attests to a certified information security management system. Green Globes attests to a recognized environmental performance standard. No tenants are published.

Within Ohio, this site holds the top rank among facilities with published megawatt figures. Those two facilities together report 23 MW total, meaning CIN5 accounts for 12 of those 23 MW, or roughly 52 percent of the state's published capacity on this site. Seventy-six facilities are mapped in Ohio, and most publish no capacity figure, so the state total is almost certainly larger than 23 MW. CIN5's position at the top of the published list reflects the limits of what operators disclose, not a confirmed dominance of Ohio's actual data center market.
